inputs.root_cause: Event 337's own exact_next_action named remove_component (Delete for non-line components) as a smaller, similarly-scoped lead worth attempting before assessing first-occurrence insertion. Design was straightforward given the 3 prior components.py functions already established the with_children()-composition pattern -- Delete needed only an omit rather than a replace.
inputs.obligation_targeted: SAL-UBL-OBL-237188D47391391E (UBL-EDIT-001) narrowed to its final, sole remaining named gap (first-occurrence insertion for a not-yet-present type); real new product code shipped, plus a genuine, surprising validate()-coverage limitation found and honestly disclosed.
inputs.acceptance_evidence: remove_component composes with_children() to omit rather than replace a child, needing no type check (nothing to validate about the shape of a REMOVED node). Reused the identical _refuse_if_worse before/after diagnostic-comparison pattern already shared by every other function in the module. During test-writing, an initial draft asserted that removing a document's own mandatory AccountingSupplierParty would be refused by validate() -- this failed when run. Investigated directly (not assumed) via a standalone probe: confirmed validate() does not check presence of ANY mandatory top-level element (IssueDate, InvoiceTypeCode, DocumentCurrencyCode, AccountingSupplierParty all XSD minOccurs=1, all missing simultaneously still reports is_valid=True). Corrected both the test and the function's own docstring (which had made the same wrong claim before being caught) to state the verified truth.

execution_steps: 1. Checked git log/status for concurrent-worker conflicts -- clean, no new commits since this session's own Event 337 commit.
2. Re-read components.py's own current state (replace_party, update_component, add_component, and the shared _refuse_if_worse helper) before designing anything new.

3. Designed remove_component(document, *, component_name, index) -> UblDocument: locate the index-th root child matching component_name by local name, refuse an out-of-range index, remove it via tuple slicing (the omit-rather-than-replace variant of with_children() every other function in this module already uses), rebuild via with_root(), run _refuse_if_worse. No type check needed since nothing about the shape of a REMOVED node requires validation (unlike replace_party/update_component/add_component, which each validate a REPLACEMENT node's own type).

4. Added the function to the SAME components.py file, updated the module docstring to describe the now-complete CRUD-for-already-present-occurrences picture. Ran mypy --strict and ruff before writing any test -- clean on the first pass.
5. Wired the export through the top-level __init__.py, ran the full ubl suite (1201 passed, unchanged) to confirm zero regression from the additive change alone.

6. Wrote a first draft of a test file including a refusal test asserting that removing a document's own only AccountingSupplierParty (confirmed via direct XSD read to be minOccurs='1', mandatory) would raise UblValidationError, reasoning by analogy that validate() would catch the resulting schema violation the same way it catches other regressions elsewhere in this session's own work.

7. Ran the test suite -- this specific test FAILED with 'DID NOT RAISE'. Did not assume the test was simply flaky or wrong without investigating: wrote a standalone Python probe loading a document missing IssueDate/InvoiceTypeCode/DocumentCurrencyCode/AccountingSupplierParty simultaneously (all XSD minOccurs='1' per direct schema read) and calling validate() directly -- confirmed is_valid=True, zero diagnostics. This is a genuine, previously-undiscovered gap in validate()'s own coverage: it does not check for mandatory top-level element presence at all, only checks things it happens to check within elements that ARE present (types, ordering, referential integrity for lines).

8. Corrected the test file: replaced the false-premise refusal test with a new test that directly documents and PROVES the actual, verified behavior (removal succeeds, the element is genuinely gone, matching what actually happens) rather than asserting a false claim -- with a detailed docstring explaining the investigation and explicitly noting this is validate()'s own scope gap, not remove_component's own defect, and not something UBL-EDIT-001 is responsible for closing.

9. Also found and corrected the IDENTICAL wrong claim already written into remove_component's own source docstring in components.py (written before the test caught the error) -- updated it to state the same verified truth rather than leave a misleading claim in the shipped API's own documentation.

10. Re-ran the corrected test file (8/8 pass), mypy --strict and ruff on both changed source files (clean), the full ubl suite again (1209 passed, was 1201), and the combined 6-format regression (4020 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed, was 4012) since production source was touched.

11. Considered whether to open a formal found-issue-register.yaml entry for the validate()-coverage gap -- decided against creating one this tick (that registry's own full lifecycle machinery, root-cause IDs, healing taskcards, is a heavier governance action than this tick's own focused CRUD scope warrants, and Rule 2's product-first/minimal-machinery guidance favors disclosing this honestly in the evidence text over spawning new governance ceremony); the finding is fully disclosed in this obligation's own ledger entry, evidence truth_boundary, and this transcript instead, discoverable by any future tick investigating validate()'s own obligation.
